historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Historical CAGRs (revenue 3yr: 41.1%, FCF 3yr: 69.7%, equity 2yr: 51.8%) reflect the 2023-2025 hypergrowth phase and are not representative of the current trajectory. FY2026 guidance of +15-18% revenue growth (midpoint 17%) is used as Year 1 because it reflects the deliberate strategic pivot to user growth over monetization. EPS CAGRs are excluded as unreliable due to the company's recent profitability inflection and a $256.7M one-time deferred tax benefit in FY2025.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical growth rates are structurally elevated and not suitable as DCF base. Revenue 3yr CAGR (41.1%) and FCF 3yr CAGR (69.7%) far exceed sustainable long-run growth. FY2026 guidance represents a significant deceleration: bookings growth slowing from 33% to 10-12%, EBITDA margins compressing ~450bps. Selected growth rate anchored to guidance, not historical CAGRs.

notes.eps_excluded: EPS CAGR unreliable: company only reached consistent profitability in FY2023-2024, and FY2025 EPS of $8.31 is inflated by a $256.7M one-time deferred tax asset release (normalized EPS ~$3.16).
notes.equity_cagr_limited: Only 2-year equity CAGR available (FY2023-FY2025) as earlier balance sheet data not in dataset. Equity CAGR of 51.8% reflects early-stage profitability buildup and is not suitable as a steady-state growth proxy.
notes.fcf_margin_note: FCF margin (34.7% of revenue in FY2025) is higher than Adj EBITDA margin (29.5%) due to favorable working capital dynamics (deferred revenue from subscriptions), minimal capex (~2.6% of revenue), and tax benefits. FY2026 FCF guided >$350M on ~$1.2B revenue (~29-30% margin floor) despite EBITDA margin compression.

base.name: Base Case: Guided Deceleration Then Recovery
base.description: FY2026 is a deliberate investment year. Revenue growth follows guidance (17%) before re-accelerating in FY2027-2028 as the expanded user base (targeting 100M DAUs from 52.7M) drives higher monetization. Growth then moderates as the company scales toward $2B+ revenue.
base.reasoning: Y1 (17%): Per FY2026 guidance midpoint. Y2-Y3 (20-22%): Re-acceleration as user growth investments pay off, DAU growth recovers, and Max tier adoption expands. Y4-Y5 (18-15%): Natural deceleration as the company approaches $1.5B-$2B revenue. FCF margin of 33% reflects structural FCF conversion advantage (deferred revenue, low capex) even as EBITDA margin is guided to compress to ~25%.

bull.name: Bull Case: Platform Shift Succeeds, DAU Target Achieved
bull.description: The AI-first strategy proves as transformative as the 2013 mobile bet. Duolingo reaches 100M DAUs ahead of schedule, driving strong bookings re-acceleration. Max tier adoption accelerates as AI features (Video Call, Roleplay) differentiate against free AI tools.
bull.reasoning: Y1 (20%): Slight beat to guidance as early investment pays off faster than expected. Y2-Y3 (28-25%): Significant re-acceleration as 100M DAU milestone drives monetization leverage. Revenue from Chess, Math, and Music begins to contribute meaningfully. Y4-Y5 (22-18%): Strong but moderating growth. FCF margin of 36% reflects operating leverage as revenue scales past $2B on a relatively fixed cost base. Lower WACC (9%) justified by stronger balance sheet and reduced execution risk.

bear.name: Bear Case: Investment Cycle Fails, Competitive Erosion
bear.description: The FY2026 investment year fails to reignite user growth. Bookings deceleration proves structural rather than strategic. AI competitors (ChatGPT, Gemini) erode Duolingo's unique value proposition faster than the company can respond. The 2026 EBITDA miss becomes a permanent margin reset.
bear.reasoning: Y1 (15%): Below guidance midpoint, at low-end of guidance range. Y2 (12%): Investment year shows limited DAU reacceleration, bookings stay depressed. Y3-Y5 (10-6%): Structural growth deceleration as market saturation, AI competition, and effectiveness concerns limit expansion. FCF margin of 28% reflects permanent margin compression as AI cost inflation offsets operating leverage. Higher WACC (11.5%) reflects elevated execution risk, CFO transition uncertainty, and potential for multiple compression.

sensitivity.matrix_note: All cells use base case growth rates [17%, 20%, 22%, 18%, 15%] with varying WACC (rows, 8-12%) and terminal growth rate (columns, 2-4%). Values are intrinsic value per share in USD. At the current price of $117.45, ALL combinations show upside. Even the most conservative scenario (WACC 12%, terminal growth 2%) implies $161.49 (+37.5% upside).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Equal probability assigned to bull and bear cases (25% each) with base case at 50%. The bear case is 25% (not higher) because: (1) the balance sheet is fortress-strong ($1.036B cash, zero debt) limiting catastrophic downside; (2) even the bear case shows positive FCF growth; (3) analyst consensus remains strongly bullish; (4) management has a track record of execution. The bull case warrants 25% weight given the validated power of prior investment cycles and the strength of the AI-driven product roadmap.

key_assumptions_summary.why_guidance_based_growth: Duolingo's 2023-2025 hypergrowth (revenue CAGR 41%, FCF CAGR 70%) was exceptional and is explicitly not the basis for this DCF. The company has communicated clearly that FY2026 is a deliberate deceleration year. Using historical CAGRs as a base would produce dramatically overvalued results disconnected from current reality. Anchoring to the 17% FY2026 guidance midpoint and modeling a recovery arc is the most analytically sound approach.
key_assumptions_summary.fcf_vs_ebitda_margin: FCF margin (33% base case) differs from Adj EBITDA margin (~25% FY2026 guidance) due to: (1) deferred revenue from annual subscriptions creates favorable working capital (~$50-80M annual benefit); (2) very low capex (~$27M in FY2025, ~2.6% of revenue); (3) continued tax benefits from deferred tax asset utilization. Consistent with FY2025 actual (FCF $360.4M = 34.7% of $1.037B revenue vs. Adj EBITDA margin of 29.5%).
key_assumptions_summary.net_cash_position: Net cash position of $1.036B (zero debt) adds significant value above enterprise value. This represents approximately $20.81 per share in cash that shareholders own above the DCF value of operations. The $400M buyback program could return ~$8.03/share to shareholders.
key_assumptions_summary.terminal_growth_justification: 3% terminal growth (base) is consistent with long-run nominal GDP growth. Online language learning market is projected to grow at 18.1% CAGR through 2035, suggesting structural tailwinds to sustain 3-4% long-term growth well beyond the 5-year projection window.
key_assumptions_summary.wacc_justification: 10% WACC reflects: risk-free rate ~4.3%, equity risk premium ~5%, beta ~1.1 (high-growth consumer tech), small size premium ~0.3%. Zero debt means WACC equals cost of equity with no leverage adjustment required.

valuation_context.peer_context: At 4x EV/Revenue for 17% growth with 25% EBITDA margins and a clean balance sheet, DUOL trades at a significant discount to historical norms and peer software companies growing at similar rates. The stock fell 78% from its May 2025 peak ($544), resetting the valuation from obviously expensive to potentially attractively valued.

analyst_consensus.note: ~23 analysts maintain Buy/Overweight ratings. Average PT ~$267 implies 127% upside from $117.45. This aligns closely with the DCF base case IV of $220.34 and probability-weighted IV of $228.81.

investment_recommendation.summary: DUOL appears significantly undervalued at $117.45 based on DCF analysis. The base case intrinsic value of $220.34 implies 88% upside. Even the bear case ($130.28) shows only 11% upside, suggesting limited downside in the worst-case scenario given the fortress balance sheet ($1.036B cash, zero debt).
investment_recommendation.bull_thesis: FY2026 investment cycle mirrors the successful 2022-2023 playbook that drove DAUs from 20M to 50M+. If the AI-first strategy works as intended, Duolingo could reach 80-100M DAUs by 2028, driving a re-acceleration in bookings and margins. The 78% decline from peak has created a rare entry point into a dominant consumer platform.
key_risks: Bookings deceleration may be structural rather than strategic: if DAU growth does not reaccelerate materially in 2026, the investment thesis breaks
AI competitors (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) improving as language tutors represents a secular competitive threat that could permanently cap user growth
CFO transition risk: Gillian Munson just started Feb 23, 2026 - days before the most consequential earnings report in company history
Current valuation still not 'cheap' on near-term metrics: ~16x FCF and ~16x EV/EBITDA for a company with decelerating growth requires execution to justify
key_catalysts: Q1 2026 earnings (May 2026): DAU reacceleration evidence would be the most important catalyst - market needs to see 20%+ DAU growth is a floor not a ceiling
Mid-year guidance update: Any raise to FY2026 bookings or EBITDA would significantly re-rate the stock
Duolingo Max tier monetization data: Evidence that premium AI features are converting at scale would validate the platform bet
Share buyback execution: $400M program represents ~7% of current market cap; aggressive buyback at current prices would be highly accretive
investment_recommendation.margin_of_safety: At $117.45, the stock trades 47% below base case IV ($220.34) and 49% below probability-weighted IV ($228.81). The $1.036B cash balance (no debt) provides a hard floor - net cash alone represents $20.81/share or 18% of current stock price. Even in the bear case, the intrinsic value ($130.28) is above current price.
